overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed Medford School Committee member Paul Ruseau about his campaign for state representative. Ruseau detailed his platform on education funding reform, single-payer healthcare, social housing, and legislative transparency.

items.title: Introduction and Favorite Dining Spots
items.summary: Host Danielle Balocca introduced school committee member Paul Ruseau, who shared his favorite local dining spots and menu items.

items.title: Decision to Run and Education Funding
items.summary: Ruseau explained that his decision to run was driven by state-level restrictions on municipal issues, highlighting school start times and the Chapter 70 school funding formula.

items.title: Healthcare Reform
items.summary: Ruseau advocated for a single-payer system and a comprehensive definition of healthcare that integrates medical, dental, mental health, and senior care.

items.title: Housing and Social Housing Model
items.summary: Ruseau argued that market-driven housing will not solve affordability crises and proposed adopting a European-style social housing model to bypass municipal restrictions.

items.title: Legislative Experience and Funding Mechanisms
items.summary: Ruseau highlighted his policy-writing record on the school committee and criticized state-level legislative clauses that make funding 'subject to appropriation.'

items.title: Coalition Building and Political Engagement
items.summary: Ruseau discussed the success of the Our Revolution Medford coalition platform and expressed concerns about Medford's representation in the district compared to Somerville.

items.title: Campaign Activities and Election Logistics
items.summary: Ruseau outlined ways for residents to volunteer and get lawn signs, noting the logistical challenges of the early September primary date.
